text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Tuesday.

LONDON - UK blue chips clawed back some of yesterday's losses to close higher albeit in very cautious trade ahead of decisions on near term interest rate policy both here and in the U.S. The FTSE 100 index finished 3.1 points higher at 4,260.9 but well off the day's best levels.

FRANKFURT - German shares ended bourse trade with small gains, German Bund market losses, which were tied to 1996 industrial production rising 1.1 percent, overshadowed the buoyant dollar, with traders seeing possible scope for correction in near-term. The 30-share DAX index ended bourse trade up 4.77 points at 3,067.06. In post-bourse trade the DAX index stood at 3,067.48.

PARIS - French stocks ended slightly lower, pressured by early weakness on Wall Street and nervousness ahead of the start of a two-day U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, traders say caution will also prevail on Wednesday as no news is expected to come from the FOMC meeting on the outlook for U.S. interest rates until late in the day. The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished down 5.48 points or 0.22 percent at 2,503.07.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended at a new record high, the fourth consecutive record closing, just a shade off the 4,300 level in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI). The market was somewhat nervous about the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee Meeting, so some profit taking could be seen off and on. The All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 5.52 points or 0.2 percent to 2,742.78.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks finished higher but well off earlier gains of three percent, brokers said short-covering of futures, by dealers especially, was inspired by the surprisingly good results of an auction on Monday of land in central Tokyo. The 225-share Nikkei average ended 228.38 points or 1.26 percent higher at 18,314.33.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks ended on a strong note, with the Hang Seng Index staging an encouraging push above 13,500 points, led by gains in the conglomerate sector. The Hang Seng index closed 97.36 points or 0.72 percent higher at 13,548.43.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market was sold down across the board, closing lower as sellers emerged to lock in profits in the absence of any countervailing overseas or local leads. The All Ordinaries index lost 17.8 points to close 2,409.1.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares held onto swift early morning gains to finish firmly up on the back of a wave of positive sentiment sweeping through the market. In a reverse of trends seen throughout much of 1996 a strong rand has boosted share prices as dealers lick their lips at the prospect of a resultant jump in corporate earnings. The All-share index was indicated up 52.5 points to 6,766.0 as Industrials put on 46.6 points to 8,108.2, Golds also had a good day with the index roaring ahead to be indicated up 49.3 points or 3.68 percent to 1,388.3.
